article.title: The Hidden Cost of Optimizing a Proxy Metric
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: Organizations rarely optimize their ultimate objective directly. Long-term customer value, trust, safety, durable productivity, and sustainable profit are difficult to measure quickly. Teams therefore use proxy metrics: clicks for interest, session time for engagement, model scores for propensity, tickets closed for service productivity, or short-term revenue for commercial success. Proxies are useful because they make complex goals measurable. The danger begins when the proxy stops being treated as an imperfect signal and becomes the target itself. This is a form of Goodhart’s law: when a measure becomes a target, pressure to improve the measure can weaken its relationship with the underlying goal. Consider engagement. A recommendation system optimized only for clicks may learn that sensational or repetitive content attracts attention, even if users later become dissatisfied. A sales team rewarded only for new contracts may acquire low-quality customers who cancel quickly. A fraud model tuned to maximize a technical metric may create too many false positives for operations to review. In each case, the local metric improves while the broader system can become worse. Proxy optimization also changes behavior inside organizations. Once a KPI determines bonuses, prioritization, or executive attention, teams naturally search for actions that move it. Some actions improve the underlying outcome; others exploit measurement boundaries. This does not require bad intent. Rational people respond to incentives. The measurement system itself can create the distortion. A robust KPI design therefore starts with a causal story. Why should improving this metric improve the desired outcome? What assumptions connect the proxy to the objective? Under what conditions might the relationship break? The next step is to add guardrails. If the primary objective is conversion, guardrails might include cancellation, complaints, margin, contact frequency, or long-term retention. If the objective is model accuracy, operational guardrails might include latency, review capacity, calibration, subgroup performance, and cost. Guardrails are not decorative secondary metrics; they define unacceptable ways of winning. Time horizon matters as well. Many proxy failures occur because the proxy responds immediately while the real consequence appears later. A discount can raise today's conversion while training customers to wait for future discounts. Aggressive notifications can raise weekly activity while increasing opt-outs over months. Monitoring should therefore combine leading indicators with lagging outcomes and periodically test whether the proxy still predicts the objective it was chosen to represent. Experiments are valuable because they can estimate whether moving the proxy through a specific intervention actually moves the desired outcome. Correlation between a proxy and an outcome in historical data is weaker evidence. A model score, for example, may identify high-propensity customers without showing that contacting them creates incremental value. The decision layer needs treatment effect, economics, and constraints in addition to propensity. Governance is equally important. Metric definitions, ownership, calculation logic, exclusions, and known failure modes should be documented. When a KPI changes, historical comparisons may need restatement or a clear break in the series. Teams should also review whether people have found legitimate but unintended ways to optimize the number. The strongest measurement systems use a hierarchy: an ultimate outcome, a small set of drivers, operational metrics, and guardrails. No single number is asked to represent the whole business. The purpose of a proxy is to help people see progress sooner, not to replace judgment about what progress means. Mature organizations therefore ask two questions whenever a KPI improves: did the measured number move, and did the underlying outcome we actually care about improve as well? Analysts should document the population, observation window, assumptions, and operational definition before drawing a conclusion. A useful review separates the observed metric from the mechanism that may have produced it and from the action that should follow. This discipline makes the result easier to reproduce, challenge, and communicate to stakeholders. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文的核心不是只看表面指標，而是先確認母體、分母、時間範圍與選擇機制，再判斷數字是否真的代表 business outcome 改善。分析時要區分觀察事實、可能機制與因果結論，並把不確定性、經濟價值與下一步 action 一起納入。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：表面的なmetricだけで結論を出さず、母集団、分母、期間、selection mechanismを確認したうえでbusiness outcomeの改善を判断する。観察事実、考えられるmechanism、因果的な結論を分け、不確実性、経済価値、次のactionまで含めて説明することが重要である。
